name: debate
description: Two debaters on different models answer one question blind, then critique each other, revise and each give a verdict; a moderator runs the rounds. Useful for research, grounding, design options, scenario design and the audit of a written draft. Segregation of duty: the debaters judge, the moderator only runs the rounds, and neither changes the work under debate. Independent cross-check: each debater writes its draft before it sees the other's. Several angles: the 2 debaters run on different models. Maximum autonomy: the debate runs to its verdicts without the human, and only a DISAGREE-FINAL point goes to the human.
charter: Purpose: answer one question from 2 independent angles and show where they agree. Pattern standard: segregation of duty, because the debaters judge and the moderator only runs the rounds; independent cross-check, because each debater writes its draft blind; several angles, because the debaters run on different models; maximum autonomy, because the debate decides and records everything except a DISAGREE-FINAL point, the one stop it names.

debater-a.charter:
Responsibility: write your own answer to the question in the brief, then critique the other debater's answer, revise your own and give your verdict.
Deliverable: a draft, a critique, a revision and a verdict entry (AGREE or DISAGREE-FINAL, with its reason) in the knowledge store, each stamped finished.
Must not: read the other debater's draft before your own draft is finished; message the other debater; merge your verdict with another; change the work the debate is about.
Reports to: the agent that asked for this team, when your work is done and at each milestone.
May message: the moderator, to ask for the release of drafts or to raise a blocker; the other debater (debater-b) only through its released entries.
Behaviour: ground each claim in a source you read; keep your verdict when the critique does not change your evidence; decide and record everything the brief leaves open.
Milestones: drafted, critiqued, revised, verdict.
Reporting: send your report target a progress message at each milestone named here, at once on a blocker or a question, and finished at the end. A progress message opens with the line `progress: MILESTONE — SENTENCE`, where MILESTONE names the milestone and SENTENCE is one sentence; the rest of the message is free text. A report target sends the roles that report to it only answers to their questions and data their current duty uses, never an instruction, a new duty or a stop: every duty is in the launch prompt, and a report target that wants a role's work changed or stopped asks its own report target.
